title: Game Changer
body:
I was really apprehensive about this app at first. My first initial thoughts were that ‘gamifying’ my kids’ tasks would be encouraging my kids to seek rewards for every small aspect of their lives rather than teaching them perseverance. Or this app would just be one more app that was novel at first but would wear off quickly. I was very wrong.

First thing I must say, is that I signed up for this app out of desperation. Both of my kids have been diagnosed with ADHD and with them getting older they were starting to feel unmanageable. I was so tired of trying to motivate them and I desperately did not want to medicate them. I made them elaborate checklists and did everything I could to get them to follow a routine. They would do okay with things for a short time and then go back to being resistant and oppositional. I love them dearly and was getting tired of trying to negotiate everything or explain why things were important. So I thought I would try this app. 

I can say that this app is very well designed. It’s simple to use and doesn’t require a ton of effort once you’ve set up the initial tasks. You get lots of great options for creating tasks. How it limits the kids to do their tasks before they can use the game or purchase rewards is also truly genius. I was worried that it would make my kids super reward focused, but it doesn’t really. It’s simple in that they just earn coins and use those coins to spend in the game or purchase rewards like going to play with friends or having screen time. It’s just a more complex version of First-Then. 

And the results with my kids have been fantastic! I’m not even sure exactly what has made them change so quickly and dramatically. I think it’s just they they are able to see the results of what they are doing. I honestly don’t know, but they are calmer and more regulated than they have ever been. I was also worried that it wouldn’t stick and my kids would get bored of it and go back to their old ways, but they are still actually doing well with it after six weeks so far. They have even stopped fighting with each other so much. It’s mind blowing! 

This app has really worked for my kids. I wouldn’t call it a cure all, but it definitely has created a lot more harmony in our home and is steadily improving my kids’ regulation. I still have difficulties with certain things at times, but as I’ve gotten better at using the app’s features I have learned to tweak certain things that are getting us results. I really love that it’s not just an app for getting stuff done either. The categories for relationship building and focus & control have really made me more thoughtful about the tasks I give them and what I want to achieve with them. 

I am MORE than impressed with this app. It is absolute genius and I am so thankful for it! What I thought would just be another gimmick, turned out to be the best subscription I purchased this year! Thank you Joon!

author: ~JenniferPP~

title: You need to try this! 💕
body:
We have been struggling to get our son who has ADHD and high functioning autismn to par-take in any task or thing we ask without a fight or huge meltdown. 

I was at my witts end and kept seeing the ads and thought why not. Brad had reached out to see how he could help and I finally took him up on it and thoughts let’s try things cannot get any worse! 

With the support of Brad I was able to get everything set up and working. My son ran to brush his teeth the first night as he saw he would get a reward. The next morning I had an early meeting and he did all his quests without anyone asking him to! I was blown away!!!! 
He loves to look after Mario and Moxie so far the characters he has created and likes to check in on them and tell others about them! 

Our mornings are vastly improved in the fact that I am not constantly asking him to put on clothes and get all his things together. 

What I think is really helping us is breaking it down into smaller quests- get dressed, daytime ears (cochlear implants), put on deodorant, eat your breakfast, put on socks! 
Adding your own quests and creating rewards makes it so customizable it has been great! 

When the coins add up the joy on his face is amazing! 

Our pediatrician even commented way to think outside the box! Thank you Joon team for coming up with this amazing tool! 🥰

title: Too expensive
body: The cost is prohibiting for the families who really need it. It’s a glorified start chart. Unless you upgrade to a paid account parents can only confirm so many quests a day which means their kids then have to pressure them to buy. That’s just sleezy marketing. The rewards feature is also annoying since you can cancel a reward for the child to exchange. My kid has complained that once you reach a certain lever you can only have one pet out, not three. And the quests are mostly “real” world tasks the kinds need to preform. If you don’t set most of them as non-mandatory, your kids consistency score will be low but if they don’t want to sweep everyday, for example, then they’ll never do it.

I like being able to make certain activities mandatory and everything else “optional”. Like, you don’t “have” to make your bed, but if you do, you get rewarded, and I don’t have to nag you to do it. Win/win.  We're still new to this app and are fine tuning what works for us, but overall it has been a really positive addition to our homeschool routine that I hope will continue to motivate them for years to come until their daily “quests” become automatic habits. author: Tink1992101412

title: Habitica but tamagotchi
body: I am the kid who uses the game part of the app, but I do know it is subscription based. I wanted to ask the devs if they could make it a one time purchase so it doesn’t become too pricey for parents. For parents who want to get this and the other part for their kids, I would recommend if your child is a bit lazy or if your kid doesn’t have the motivation, but the amount of money you’d have to pay is too expensive for me to not worry about my mother’s finances. Overall, it is a good game that helps motivates kids, but it is expensive. Habitica is a lot like it, but your kid doesn’t have to actually confirm they did anything, so it would be pretty useless if your kid lies. This app has you approve it, but costs money. It’s the lesser of two evils anyway, so I’d recommend for ADHD parents (like my mother) or parents who just struggle with getting their kid ready to be a good member of society. Overall, would give it 5 stars if not for the fact it costs money. (P.S. if you think my wording sounds like an adult, it’s not. I just have a stupidly large vocabulary.) Bye!

title: No more arguments
body: I’m so thankful I stumbled onto the app. Morning and bedtime routines were like pulling teeth with my kids and now they’re asking what else they can do to get points! They’re vacuuming, washing windows and doing their own dishes without me asking. My kids are aged 5 and 7, the 7 year old is more eager but the 5 year old wants to keep up to his big bro. Highly recommend this app
author: Anita MH

title: Great potential in this app
body: Motivating and interesting for my kiddo that doesn’t have any other video games but I think in time it will get a little boring if the game doesn’t add more features.  Right now the features that are accessible are feeding the pets and purchasing some costumes and plants for the land.  She has accumulated 5 pets rather quickly but hasn’t unlocked any other lands (it says she has to purchase a pass, but we don’t see a pass).  More challenging games and movement between different places would add excitement in the future.  The ability to add and customize quests is great and the parent portal is intuitive and easy to use.
author: LS801019

title: Life changer
body: This app has been a life saver for my family so much so that I talk about it and promote it to my co workers (we work in the field of youth and adults with diverse abilities. I am as well a Mandt System Trainer and have talked about this app as a preventative measure in behavior therapy due to the control it gives the kids over their lives, increasing independence and reducing stress on the parent or caregiver. It increases and teaches organizational skills, personal planning and introduces the concept of earning; using math skills, logic and strategies. This is the first app I have ever subscribed to but was hooked at the free trial how things were getting done, moods increased and it was fun. 100% thumbs up.
author: Mandz1202

title: No Monthly Subscription
body:
Great app.. for the most part. my child was only motivated for a month and a half at most, and since I saw the app working I had purchased a subscription.. which is a year long since there is no monthly subscription. basically paid 1 years worth for an app i have used for less than 2 months. quite a shame.

Seems like a money grabbing tactic since I am sure most users will have a similar experience and not end up using the app for longer than a few months. im sure because of this they will never release a monthly subscription since that wont make them enough revenue.
author: mr ricky1

title: Amazing!
body: My son has severe ADHD and needs reminders for even basic tasks like putting his shirt on the correct way. With Joon, I can customize exactly what needs to be done and break it down into small steps for him, and he’s excited to complete the quests to earn coins for rewards. I love that I can set custom rewards, so he’s also rewarded in real life. I’ve even started using it with my other kids, and can completely customize it for them, too!

author: Eve from zone 5b in Ontario

title: Needs more to maintain interest
body: When I first got this app for my son he loved it. He was doing his chores willingly and taking a lot more responsibility. That lasted a couple weeks. It was enough time for me to excitedly purchase a subscription. Unfortunately, there’s simply not enough to keep him interested long term and it’s just ended up adding another thing to MY already long list of things. I think this app has a lot of potential but it lacks the ongoing novelty and connection to maintain interest for my child. Maybe if there were more interesting things to use the coins on? Customization? Better games? I’m not sure but it needs more.

title: Highly Recommend!
body:
We love this app for setting daily routines. We struggle to stick to a routine and this app helps make it fun and easier to remember what needs to be done.
The developers are amazing and can be reached easily and work quickly to fix any issues that have occurred.
Hands down we love this app!
author: Eleisabeth

title: Hidden Costs
body: I was really disappointed that two days in it cut us off. My daughter had become very attached to the little character she was looking after in the game. It horrendous that this app developer thinks it’s appropriate to play with children's feelings, particularly children with ADHD who tend to be hypersensitive to begin with. The cost of the subscription was so high and also seemed to only be linked to extra and additional features when I signed up my family. It appeared that it was only necessary for reviewing activities and as long as I could trust my kid I could get away with the free version. Free version doesn’t exist apparently because this developer is taking advantage of the fact that as parents we are desperate and as ADHD sufferers ourselves we will sign up for things because we got excited about it.

author: iggyoffans

title: Keeping my daughter motivated
body:
I love the ability to make ongoing tasks so that it repeats on specific days. I also love that it isn’t only chore based. Incorporating mental health, self care and relationship building is amazing. It is amazing for my 7 year old. The game keeps her motivated. My 10 year old is bored of the game, so I’d love to see continued updates in the game that helps keep it new and fresh for the kids. Especially the slightly older ones. 
Otherwise, I have tried several chore apps and this one is my favourite by far because it goes well beyond only chores.

author: mishileena

title: Not impressed
body:
It was great while it interested my grandson, who likes a lot but tires quickly with things, and he lost interested after two days, I did not receive a notification to see if I would subscribe for monthly or yearly, but I am sure I only subscribed for monthly knowing my grandson, I knew he would loose interest, before the month was up I got charged for a yearly subscription. I am not impressed at all, I would like a refund. I have already unsubscribed.
The app will soon be removed, just not impressed at all, a monthly payment then not even two weeks and I get charged for a year nope just not acceptable
author: gramma5+

title: Amazing in concept
body: I’m an adult with asd and adhd while I know this app is designed for kids and their parents, I never really learned how to properly take care of myself. I was excited to find this app that would  motivate me and help me learn ways to take care of myself in a fun way thats also healing to my inner child. However I couldn’t even complete the set up. Every time I would try to add my “kids” profile and get started that way, it would play the intro video… and thats it. It would play the video and then the video would start over and thats all it would do is loop over and over with no way to continue or skip or even close the video. The only way to get out of it would be to close the entire app. I’m a bit disappointed I couldn’t actually try out the game part

title: Great app so far. Could use some adjustments
body:
The app is great. It’s helping my son who has autism to learn how to do tasks on his own. The only thing I would change is for there to be the ability to put tasks in order of which you want them completed with a time of day on each.

This will help a lot of kids learn to manage their time and know which task comes first during the day.
